# motion-harness

> Eyes and hands for AI agents that make videos. A CLI (`mh`) next to a React video project: the timeline as data, check frames in seconds, a DOM probe, lints before and after rendering, motion and audio as numbers, a native renderer that needs no Remotion, stills, subtitles, per-platform deliveries, and a review player whose comments come back as scene and frame.

## Start

- [README](README.md): what it is, install, the loop
- [The skill](skills/motion-harness/SKILL.md): how an agent works on a film with it
- [Feedback skill](skills/motion-harness-feedback/SKILL.md): a human's comment to a verified edit
- [Sound skill](skills/motion-harness-sound/SKILL.md): music, sfx, voice, loudness
- [Deliver skill](skills/motion-harness-deliver/SKILL.md): the handover
- [Motion graphics skill](skills/motion-harness-mograph/SKILL.md): a film as data, edited by address, drawn by the harness
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): working in this repository

## Reference

- `mh help`: every command with its flags
- Motion graphics as data: `mh new --mograph`, `mh layers`, `mh set <scene>.<layer>.<prop> <value>`, `mh key`, `mh add`, `mh layout`, `mh edit` ([docs/mograph.md](docs/mograph.md))
- Any film: `mh ingest --transcribe --look` probes footage (streams, silences, bars, words, the subject's box), `mh new --assets` scripts and scaffolds from it (text, clip, image scenes; voice and music cues; the subject stays in every crop)
- [Config template](templates/harness.config.ts): what a project declares
- [Timeline schema](src/timeline/schema.ts): parts, scenes, events, audio cues, rules, i18n
- [Engine interface](src/render/engine.ts): remotion or native
- [Example project](examples/basic): a film that runs through every command

## Rules an agent should know

- Addresses, not guesses: `scene+local`, `20.5s`, `f616`, `probe.pick1`; `mh resolve` translates
- Never claim a visual change without a frame or a sheet from `mh frame` or `mh check`
- Timing lives in the timeline, sound in its cues, cursor targets in `mh cursor`
- `--json` on stdout is for machines, everything else is on stderr
- Receipts in `<cache>/receipts/` say what a command produced and from which sources
